versions.short: The bill would reauthorize and update the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Chesapeake Bay Office, which would be headed by a Director with research or resource management experience in the bay. It would direct the office to use peer review to ensure funded projects are scientifically sound and to stay consistent with the Chesapeake Executive Council's agreements and priorities. The office would be able to support an integrated system of ocean and water monitoring for the bay and to build a buoy-based observing network along the Captain John Smith Chesapeake National Historic Trail. It would also allow a Chesapeake Bay watershed education and training program with grants for classroom learning, teacher training, and student internships. A further program would support restoring and managing bay habitats and living resources such as oysters, blue crabs, salt marshes, and fish species. The office would report to Congress every two years on its activities and on progress protecting the bay's living resources and habitat.
